full_judgment:
2. Defendant No. 1, the present appellant contested the suit asserting, inter alia, that the suit was not maintainable and that the alleged management committee was not legally constituted and that plaintiff No. 1 had no locus standi to file the suit; that the deity's sebait Krishna Prosanna Das Baisnab settled the suit land with defendant No. 1 on receipt of a salami of Tk. 500/- at an annual rent of Tk. 15/- after receiving a kabuliyat, executed by defendant No. 1 on 4th Asher 1360 B.S. and granting a patta to him on the following day. It was asserted that the settlement was for legal necessity for the repair of the akhra, construction of a Matmandir and for re-excavation of an old tank. Defendant No. 1's further case is that the akhra was subsequently gutted by fire and the deity was destroyed and that the sebait Krishna Prosanna left for India after appointing Gabinda Das Baisnab as the sebait and that plaintiff No. 1 Monindra Lay Roy, in the name of the allegedly constituted management committee, falsely instituted the case for harassing defendant No. 1. 

 15. In the instant case if the appellant's case is believed then the disputed settlement was accompanied by the receipt of a kabuliyat, the granting of a patta and fixation of an annual rent. No doubt that transaction resulted in a permanent alienation. Such an alienation could only be made for the legal necessity of the deity or for the benefit of the deity's property. The questioned settlement was found by both the trial court and the appellate court as bad in law on two grounds—it was a collusive transaction and, further, it was not done for the legal necessity of the deity. The appellate court found over writings on the patta and on the rent-receipts.  The patta was neither registered nor written on a stamp paper. The appellate court upheld the findings of the trial court that defendant No. 1 along with other defendants came ever the suit land in 1363 B.S. for first time and, in collusion with Krisrsna prasanna, obtained a rent-receipt and a patta for grabbing some of the akhra properties; and that the settlement, allegedly for raising money for the construction of a natmandir and other huts and for execution of a silted-up tank, was not done for legal necessity of the deity. No wonder no argument was advanced before the High Court Division with regard to the merit of the settlement, We find no substance in this appeal and, accordingly, it is dismissed with costs.
